sentences.text: This dinosaur featured a massive quadrupedal body supported by a large bony frill and three prominent skull horns.
Its sturdy build included strong limbs, short hands with three hooves, and short feet ending in four hooves.
The largest known skull, identified as specimen MWC 7584, measured 2.5 meters in length when complete.
Covering most of the body were large basement scales, the biggest known among ceratopsians, reaching up to 9 cm across.
Triceratops was a giant creature, growing to lengths of 8 to 9 meters and weighing between 6 and 10 metric tons.
One specific individual named Kelsey measured 22 to 24 feet long with a 6.5-foot skull and stood 7.5 feet tall.
Another famous specimen, Big John, was estimated to be 26.1 feet long and 10 feet tall.
The fossilized skin of a specimen named Lane was preserved through a unique process called clay templating.
This animal holds the title of official state fossil for South Dakota and the official state dinosaur for Wyoming.
The genus Triceratops was first formally described in 1889 by the American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
The initial fossil specimen attributed to this genus was discovered by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887.
Between 1889 and 1891, John Bell Hatcher collected thirty-one additional skulls of the species.
As herbivores, these animals primarily consumed low-growing vegetation but could potentially knock down taller plants using their horns, beak, and bulk.
They possessed between 432 and 800 teeth in total, with only a fraction in use at any time due to continuous replacement throughout their lives.
The jaws ended in a deep, narrow beak thought to be better adapted for stripping and browsing than for biting.
While Triceratops was certainly quadrupedal, there is debate regarding its posture, with some believing its front legs sprawled at a considerable angle to support the head's weight.
Remains of a Triceratops group show signs of predation or scavenging by Tyrannosaurus, including breakage and puncture wounds on the front limbs of the largest specimen.
A 2020 study described co-ossified tail vertebrae in Triceratops, suggesting the condition arose after one individual stepped on the tail of another.
Paleontologist Peter Dodson estimates that a Triceratops could successfully defend itself against a bull Tyrannosaurus by inflicting fatal wounds with its sharp horns.
Tyrannosaurus is known to have consumed Triceratops, evidenced by a heavily tooth-scored Triceratops ilium and sacrum.
Researchers suggest that the bone in ceratopsian skulls is metaplastic, allowing it to change shape over time.
The first extensive study of growth patterns in this dinosaur was published in 2006 in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society.
Triceratops is classified as a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur.
T. horridus is the type species of Triceratops, originally described as Ceratops by Marsh in 1889.
Thomas Lehman defined the subfamilies in 1990 and diagnosed Triceratops as a ceratopsine based on several morphological features.
Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
It lived approximately 69 to 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian age.
Triceratops lived in environments consisting of floodplains and inland forests.
Isotopic analysis suggests Triceratops specimens from the Darnell Triceratops Bonebed likely inhabited freshwater floodplains, though they were probably not restricted to a single environment.

There is an ongoing debate regarding the function of Triceratops' frill and horns, with traditional views favoring defense against predators and recent interpretations suggesting roles in species identification, courtship, and dominance displays.
In 1986, John Ostrom and Peter Wellnhofer proposed that all Triceratops remains belong to a single species, T. horridus.
Researchers suggest it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections on Triceratops feature scales bore bristles, unlike those found in other ceratopsians.
Torosaurus is distinguished by an elongated skull and two oval openings in its frill.
